external_level_conclusion: External sources help define what alpha means at a scale/scheme, but none can select the MTT source value.

sources.too_constrained_risk: A source theory may emit a more primitive normalization that must be mapped to PDG schemes.
sources.too_loose_risk: Using PDG numerical inputs would just reproduce measured SM parameters.
sources.use: Defines electroweak context, SU(2)xU(1) couplings, weak mixing, and input-scheme/radiative-correction discipline.

sources.too_constrained_risk: A high-scale/source alpha result should not be rejected merely because low-energy running is not yet computed.
sources.too_loose_risk: Hadronic running data cannot be used to select MTT source strength.
sources.use: Confirms alpha and weak mixing angle running depend on hadronic vacuum polarization/current correlator data.

sources.too_constrained_risk: It targets precision SM prediction, while this repo first needs source normalization.
sources.too_loose_risk: Measured cross sections are comparison inputs, not no-knob derivation.
sources.use: Shows alpha(M_Z) predictions include hadronic vacuum-polarization and cross-section data.

sources.too_constrained_risk: Demanding one convention too early may hide the primitive MTT source coordinate.
sources.too_loose_risk: A 5/3 factor or string-inspired normalization cannot be imported without selected operator data.
sources.use: Illustrates that U(1)/hypercharge normalization is model-dependent and often GUT-normalized.
